text.p: A Filipino-Chinese realtor was rescued on Wednesday by government troops in the southern Philippines a day after he was kidnapped by three men disguised as preachers, police said.

Raymundo Tan, who was abducted on Tuesday in Iligan City on Mindanao island, was abandoned in a mosque as his kidnappers fled after a brief gun battle with a pursuing team of police and military personnel, Police major Pablo Arnado said.
Arnado said Tan was unharmed by the kidnappers who fled in a vehicle provided by a town mayor negotiating his release.
Describing to reporters how he was moved from place to place during his captivity, Tan said: "It was mostly a mountain climbing experience. And the climb was like hell."
Police said the kidnappers had earlier demanded a ransom of five million pesos ($190,000), but it was not clear if they received any money.
Tan's abduction was the second this week.

On Sunday, suspected Moslem guerrillas kidnapped Japanese businessman Kenichi Takayama and three Filipinos from a beach resort on Sarangani island, 320 km (200 miles) southeast of Iligan. They shot dead another Filipino on the beach.
Pursuing soldiers rescued Takayama and the others on Monday after killing two of the kidnappers in a gunbattle.
More than 40 people have been abducted since January in the Mindanao region, which is home to Moslem guerrillas fighting for an Islamic state.
